title: Vault-specific CLI interface so you don't need to interact with cryfs, encfs, gocryptfs etc binaries directly
line: A new plasma-vault command lists, unlocks and locks vaults from a terminal, asking for the password in the usual Plasma Vault dialog.
explanation: From a terminal, vaults could only be driven through qdbus with the encrypted folder's full path; qdbus can't even print the vault list (a(sssqsasb)), and the service never filled in the mount point in the vault info it sends. Force locking was also broken: forceClose() started the unmount before the onSuccess handler that kills the apps had run, so the apps died but the vault stayed mounted. The new plasma-vault tool (list, open <vault>, close [--force] <vault>, close --all) talks to the existing kded D-Bus service, accepts a vault name, mount point or encrypted folder, and waits for locking to finish so it can report the reason and exit with 1 on failure; unlocking asks for the password in the service's own dialog, so no password ever goes through the command line (Ivan's concern in comment 3). The service now sends the mount point, and forceClose() kills the apps first and waits up to 2 s for them to exit before unmounting.

commits.message:
cli: add a plasma-vault command line tool

Vaults could only be locked or unlocked from a terminal through qdbus
and the encrypted folder path. The new tool lists, unlocks and locks
vaults by name or path, and force locking now kills apps before unmount.

BUG: 438070

media.caption: Master: there is no plasma-vault command, qdbus can't list the vaults, and openVault by name silently does nothing
With the change: plasma-vault list shows the vault, and plasma-vault open Notes brings up the usual unlock dialog
Master: forceCloseVault kills the app using the vault, but the vault stays mounted
With the change: close reports the app using the vault and exits 1; close --force kills it and locks the vault
